title: Country
description: One ISO 3166-1 entry (sovereign state or dependent territory). Region-level content (climate, cuisine, sports, etc.) never lives here — it always lives in distinct-regions/*.yaml, even for countries with a single synthetic whole-country region.

alpha3.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code. Primary key of this entry.

alpha2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Also the namespace prefix used by ISO 3166-2 subdivision codes.

local.description: The country's name, one entry per language that has a languageUsage[] row with domain: official (e.g. CHE has 4: deu/fra/ita/roh; LTU has 1: lit). Not a place to force every language baboratory.com might translate the site into; that's a separate concern from this core dataset. See region.schema.json's name.local[] for the same field at region level, where it means something narrower (locally used there specifically, not every official language of the whole country).

languageCode.description: ISO 639-3 code, e.g. fra, tah, mri

isSovereign.description: false for dependent territories / special administrative regions (e.g. PYF, HKG, GRL).

governanceType.description: Drives the region-splitting rule: federal and unitary-large countries have real ISO 3166-2 subdivisions in distinct-regions[]; unitary-small and dependent-territory countries have exactly one synthetic whole-country region.

iso3166_2_prefix.description: Equals alpha2 when this country has real subdivisions (hasSubdivisions=true). Null otherwise. Kept as an explicit field rather than re-deriving from alpha2, so consumers don't need to know the governanceType rule to build a subdivision code.

hasSubdivisions.description: true only for federal and unitary-large countries with real ISO 3166-2 regions. false means distinct-regions[] holds a single synthetic whole-country entry.

languageUsage.description: Flat (languageCode, domain, speakersShare) rows describing a country's language situation. One language can appear multiple times with different domains (e.g. an official language that is also widely locally spoken). Per-language display name / basic phrases live in data/languages/<code>.yaml, not here.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-3 code. Must have a matching data/languages/<code>.yaml entry.

domain.description: official = de jure official languages. locallySpoken = languages spoken by the local/resident population (native + minority languages). foreign = languages spoken as a learned second/foreign language.

speakersShare.description: Meaning depends on domain. For 'official': always 1.0 for every de jure official language, regardless of how many the country has — this is a legal-status flag, not a population measurement, so it is never split across co-official languages (e.g. a country with 4 official languages lists all 4 at 1.0, not 0.25 each). Actual usage of an official language is captured separately via a 'locallySpoken' entry for the same languageCode. For 'locallySpoken'/'foreign': true proportion of the relevant population who speaks the language; entries need not sum to 1 across a domain (bilingualism, rounding).

variant.description: Optional BCP47-style region subtag (base language ISO 639-1/2 code, not the ISO 639-3 languageCode above, since that's the established regional-variant convention — e.g. 'fr-FR' vs 'fr-CA', 'es-ES' vs 'es-AR') when it matters which regional variant is meant. Deliberately narrow: this is a variant *label*, not a catalog of slang/idiom/taboo-word differences between variants — that's a much bigger, harder-to-verify undertaking and out of scope here.

currency.description: The country's currency. One currency object per entry — territories that informally circulate a second currency (e.g. USD alongside a local currency) note that in a free-text way isn't modeled here yet; add a note to 'name' if it matters until this needs to become an array.

code.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. EUR, USD, XPF.

legalConstraints.description: Regulatory/legal facts relevant to an AI agent doing e-commerce, marketing, data-collection, or consulting tasks for this country — data-collection restrictions (e.g. why ethnicGroups/religions might be absent here), consumer-rights basics, price-display rules (VAT-inclusive vs. exclusive), trading-hours restrictions, etc. Each entry needs an official legal source, same as any other statistical/factual claim in this dataset.

topic.description: Short label, e.g. 'ethnicity/religion data collection', 'VAT price display', 'Sunday trading'.

paymentMethodShares.description: Statistical adoption/usage share of payment methods, in percent. Like other statistical fields, requires an official source (central bank, national payment association) per entry.

paymentCulture.description: Qualitative payment/financial customs — deliberately no sourceId requirement (these are customary norms, not census-style statistics; cite a sourceId on a field only when a specific claim genuinely has an authoritative source behind it).

popularMethods.description: Locally prominent payment brands/rails worth knowing about even without a hard percentage, e.g. specific card networks or local payment apps.

typicalAmount.description: Free text, e.g. '5-10%', 'round up the bill'.

autoIncludedInBill.description: Whether a service charge is customarily/legally already added to the bill.

communicationStyle.description: Qualitative communication/social-etiquette notes. No sourceId requirement — these are cultural generalizations (with the usual caveat that any national-level generalization is an approximation, not a rule every individual follows), not statistics.

contextLevel.description: Hall's framework: low-context = direct, explicit communication is the norm (e.g. Germany); high-context = meaning relies more on shared context, indirectness, reading between the lines (e.g. Japan). A simplification, not a strict rule.

formalityNorms.description: Address forms, titles, when/whether to move to a first-name basis.

meetingEtiquette.description: Punctuality expectations, who speaks/decides, business-card exchange, pace of decision-making.

ethnicGroups.description: National minorities / ethnic composition, in percent.

name.description: IANA tz database name, e.g. Europe/Paris

standardUtcOffset.description: UTC offset outside daylight saving time (standard/winter time).

observesDst.description: Whether this timezone shifts for daylight saving time at all — many do not (most of the tropics, some entire countries like Japan or China).

dstUtcOffset.description: UTC offset while daylight saving time is in effect. Required (checked by scripts/validate.py, not JSON Schema alone) when observesDst=true; must be absent when observesDst=false.

dstPeriod.description: Roughly when DST applies, in plain terms (e.g. 'Last Sunday of March to last Sunday of October, EU-wide schedule'). Required (checked by scripts/validate.py) when observesDst=true. Deliberately free text rather than exact dates — the rule (not the specific date) is usually what's stable, and DST start/end dates shift yearly (last-Sunday-of-month style) or even get abolished by legislation.

distinct-regions.description: References to files under distinct-regions/. Not an exhaustive list of the country's administrative subdivisions — only the ones curated in this dataset (e.g. FRA currently documents 2 of its ~18 regions). Every country's list contains exactly one entry with code 'WHOLE' (checked by scripts/validate.py, not JSON Schema alone) — for hasSubdivisions=false countries it is the only entry; for hasSubdivisions=true countries it sits alongside the real ISO 3166-2 entries as the generic country-wide fallback content used when a visitor's specific subdivision isn't curated (see usage_examples/python/get_data_by_ip.py).

code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code, or the synthetic value 'WHOLE' for the always-present generic/country-wide entry.

file.description: Relative path to the region YAML file.

adminUnitCodes.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code(s) this curated region maps to, for IP-geolocation-based region lookup (most IP geolocation databases — MaxMind GeoIP2, DB-IP, IP2Location — report a subdivision's ISO 3166-2 code; MaxMind's raw 'iso_code' field omits the country prefix, e.g. 'BRE', so prefix it with alpha2 to get 'FR-BRE'). Required (checked by scripts/validate.py, not JSON Schema) on every non-WHOLE entry of a hasSubdivisions=true country — normally the same single value as 'code', list more than one only if this curated region's boundary spans multiple official ISO 3166-2 subdivisions. Always omitted on the WHOLE entry (in every country, regardless of hasSubdivisions) — WHOLE is the generic/country-wide fallback, it does not represent one specific admin unit, so there is nothing to match against.

sources.description: Registry of official sources backing the statistical fields in this file (ethnicGroups, languageUsage, legalConstraints, paymentMethodShares). Every sourceId used below must have a matching entry here — checked by scripts/validate.py, not by JSON Schema alone.

id.description: Unique within this file. Referenced by sourceId fields elsewhere in the same file.

name.description: Title of the specific document/dataset/page, e.g. '2021 Population and Housing Census'.

publisher.description: The official body, e.g. 'Statistics Lithuania (Valstybės duomenų agentūra)', 'CIA World Factbook'.

year.description: Year the underlying data refers to (not necessarily the access date).

accessedDate.description: Date this source was consulted, YYYY-MM-DD.

note.description: Exactly what in this file was taken from this source, e.g. 'ethnicGroups percentages' or 'languageUsage locallySpoken shares for lit/rus/pol'.

sourceIdRef.description: Must match a sources[].id declared in this same file.
